# `returndensity`: point density and first-return share {#sec-returndensity}

## What it does

`returndensity` maps how many returns fell in each cell per unit area,
and what percent of them were first returns. Density maps are the
standard check that an acquisition meets its specified point density.
Low-density patches, stripes from overlapping flight lines, and water
drop-outs all show up here. The first-return percent is lower under dense
canopy, where each pulse produces several returns.

## Example commands

{{< include ../examples/fragments/returndensity_commands.md >}}

## Options used

| Option | Value | What it does |
|:--------|:--------------------|:-------------------------|
| `/output` | `out/returndensity.tif` | The two-band density raster. |
| `/cellsize` | `10` | Cell size, 10 ft. Larger cells give smoother density estimates. |

: Options used in the `returndensity` example. {#tbl-options-returndensity}

## Outputs

One GeoTIFF with two bands:

- `point_density`: returns per square unit of the input's coordinate
  system (per square foot for the example tile).
- `first_return_ratio_pct`: first returns as a percent of all returns.

## Results

@fig-returndensity-maps shows both bands. Density is fairly even. The
first-return percent stays between 0 and 100 and is lowest where the
canopy is densest.

{{< include ../examples/fragments/returndensity_figures.md >}}

## Checks

@tbl-checks-returndensity confirms that each cell's count matches R
exactly, that density times cell area adds back up to the tile's point
count, that the first-return percent stays between 0 and 100, and that
the band's unit label names the tile's own units (feet).

{{< include ../examples/fragments/returndensity_checks.md >}}
